candidates.name: Maya Chen

application.shipped_thing: https://github.com/mayac/quietnotes — a journaling app I shipped in 2025. Around 200 daily users. Built solo. Taught me that the writing prompt matters more than the AI behind it.
application.ai_workflow: Cursor + Claude Sonnet for code, occasionally Opus for architecture. I keep a tools.md per project where I track which prompts worked. Local Ollama for stuff I want offline.
application.ai_collaborator_story: On Quietnotes, I was stuck on how to handle journaling streaks without making them feel like a guilt-trip metric. I had a 90-minute conversation with Claude where I argued *against* my own design and it pushed back on me until I landed on a 'witnessed days' frame instead of a streak. The product is better for it. AI was a sparring partner, not a code monkey.
application.what_to_build: An AI agent that runs co-op governance — meeting facilitation, conflict surfacing, decision tracking — for small worker-owned businesses.
application.lens_fit: Regenerative + sovereignty. Co-ops keep wealth in the community and give workers agency. AI usually helps capital concentrate; this would do the opposite. The third lens (consciousness) shows up in the conflict-surfacing piece — making invisible group dynamics visible to the group.
application.why_this: Because I want to spend my next 10 weeks building something I actually believe in, with people who think AI should make humans more, not less. I'm tired of building productivity tools for venture-scale loneliness.

candidates.name: Sage Whitman

application.availability: Conditional — I have a part-time consulting commitment 8 hrs/week that I cannot break, but the other 32 hrs are yours.
application.shipped_thing: https://earthsystems.coop/dashboard — climate-data dashboard for regenerative agriculture co-ops in the Rocky Mountain west. About 15 farms use it weekly. Open source: github.com/earthsys/dashboard.
application.ai_workflow: Pretty light. I use ChatGPT for first drafts and Claude for thinking through hard design decisions. I'm not deeply AI-native yet — that's part of why I'm applying. I want to get fluent with AI as a co-builder, not as a tool.
application.ai_collaborator_story: Honest answer: I haven't yet had the experience your prompt is asking about. I've used AI to write code faster, but I haven't experienced it as a collaborator in the way the studio describes. I'd like to learn that.
application.what_to_build: An AI watershed steward — pulls in real-time water/soil/biodiversity data for a watershed, surfaces what humans should pay attention to, drafts the governance decisions for co-op members to vote on. Tools that help humans steward land at the scale of a watershed instead of a parcel.
application.lens_fit: Regenerative is the obvious one — direct ecological work. Sovereignty fits because data stays with the watershed community. Consciousness fits in the deepest sense: it's about expanding human attention to the non-human world.
application.why_this: I run a small co-op. We have land work to do. AI could 10x our capacity if we knew how to wield it. I want to come back from the studio with the fluency to do that, and a tool that other co-ops can use.
application.equity_ok: yes — though I'd want to discuss how the IP works if the tool ends up being shared across our co-op network
application.other: I'm older than most applicants probably (39). Been building tech in service of regenerative work for 12 years. If that's a fit issue, just tell me.
